segments.text: In the voice house, everyone was asleep, except Pip, the smallest pillow on the sofa.
Nell? Nell, are you awake? The lamp in the hallway is humming and I can't stop listening to it.
Pip tiptoed up the stairs, past 40 sleeping portraits, all the way to the attic door.
Who goes there at this hour of the night?
It's only me, Professor Hoot. The hallway lamp won't stop humming.
Hmm. Lamps don't hum for nothing, little one. Lamps hum when they're lonely.
Lonely. Just then, a tiny voice squeaked from inside the pantry.
Lonely. I'll keep it company. I've got crumbs and I know three songs.
So the three of them sat beneath the hallway lamp and Tilly sang her first song about cheese.
Oh, cheddar in the morning and brie before bed.
That is a terrible song. Sing it again.
She sang it again and the lamp hummed a little softer. Her second song was about the moon.
The moon is a cracker. The moon is a cracker. Nibble it slowly and the night gets darker.
Look, it's flickering. I think it's laughing.
And by her third song, the lamp's hum had turned into a gentle purr like a cat full of milk.
There, nobody likes to be the only one awake.
Pip curled up on the hall rug.
Hoot tucked his head under his wing until he fell asleep mid-chorus.
And the lamp, glowing softly, watched over all of them until morning.
I'll see you next time.
